summary: Defines the Network Control Protocol for establishing and configuring AppleTalk over PPP. The RFC has historic status.

eli5.summary: This lets Apple's old networking language ride over a PPP phone-line connection, with both ends agreeing on settings first.

questions: how does appletalk work over ppp
subtitle: Configure Apple's old networking protocol over phone-line connections.

tldr.problem: AppleTalk networks needed a way to establish and configure connections over point-to-point links like phone lines, with both ends agreeing on settings.
tldr.mechanism: The AppleTalk Control Protocol (ATCP) acts as a network control protocol within PPP, negotiating configuration options such as network addresses, routing protocols, and broadcast suppression before AppleTalk datagrams can flow.
tldr.outcome: AppleTalk can operate over PPP links in three modes: dial-in end systems, router-to-router with network numbers, and half-router connections without assigned network numbers. This RFC is Historic.

today: RFC 1378 is a Historic protocol. AppleTalk and PPP dial-up connections have been superseded by modern networks and broadband, but the specification remains available for systems that must maintain legacy AppleTalk connectivity.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The AppleTalk Control Protocol (ATCP) is a network control protocol (NCP) that works within PPP (Point-to-Point Protocol) to establish and configure AppleTalk communications over point-to-point links.

PPP itself has three parts: a method to wrap network data over serial links, a Link Control Protocol (LCP) for setting up the physical connection, and a family of Network Control Protocols for different network layers. ATCP is the NCP for AppleTalk. Before any AppleTalk traffic can flow, both ends of the link must first use LCP to establish the data link, then ATCP to configure AppleTalk-specific parameters.
sections.eli5: Before you can send Apple network messages over a phone line, both ends need to say hello to each other and agree on how things will work. ATCP is that conversation.

sections.title: ATCP Operation
sections.content:
ATCP uses the same packet exchange mechanism as LCP, with codes for configure requests, acknowledgments, negative acknowledgments, rejections, and termination. The protocol operates during the network-layer phase of PPP, after LCP has established the connection.

AppleTalk datagrams are encapsulated in PPP frames with protocol type 0x0029. Each datagram uses an extended DDP (Datagram Delivery Protocol) header. Because AppleTalk has no standard fragmentation mechanism, PPP links supporting AppleTalk must allow at least 599 octets (the maximum DDP datagram length) in the information field.

The protocol also supports a half-router model where two AppleTalk routers link across the PPP connection without assigned node IDs or network numbers, incrementing hop counts for routing updates as they pass through.
sections.eli5: ATCP packets say 'here's what I want', 'I agree', 'I don't agree', or 'I'm closing down'. After agreement, AppleTalk messages flow across the link, with each message up to 599 bytes.

sections.title: Configuration Options
sections.content:
ATCP defines eight configuration options that peers negotiate:

AppleTalk-Address (Type 1) negotiates the network and node numbers for each end of the link. Both sides must agree on a common network number, but each must have a unique node number; network numbers can be zero but node numbers must be non-zero. Links must have non-extended characteristics.

Routing-Protocol (Type 2) specifies how routing updates flow: no routing (0), AppleTalk RTMP (1), AppleTalk AURP (2), or AppleTalk ABGP (3). RTMP is the default.

Suppress-Broadcasts (Type 3) lets one end prevent broadcast datagrams of specific DDP types from crossing the link, useful for dial-in systems to filter broadcasts from the remote network.

AT-Compression-Protocol (Type 4) negotiates compression for the AppleTalk traffic. Server-information (Type 6) and Zone-Information (Type 7) are informational only, provided by one end and not negotiated. Default-Router-Address (Type 8) gives a dial-in client the address of a router to use when both ends are end systems.
sections.eli5: These options let the two ends agree on network numbers, how to share routing news, what broadcasts to skip, whether to squeeze the data, and server details.

sections.title: Three Modes of Operation
sections.content:
ATCP supports three distinct operating modes, each requiring different configuration options.

End System to Intermediate System (dial-in mode) connects an end system client to a router. The client must negotiate an AppleTalk address and must request no routing protocol (to prevent the dial-in client from propagating routing updates). Other options like broadcast suppression and compression are optional.

Intermediate System to Intermediate System with network number connects two routers across a WAN link where the connection has an assigned network number. Both routers may negotiate a routing protocol and optional broadcast suppression.

Intermediate System to Intermediate System without network number (half-router mode) connects two routers without assigning a network number to the link itself. Both sides set their network and node numbers to zero, and typically suppress all broadcasts.
sections.eli5: Three ways to use it: a client calling a server, two routers with a named network between them, or two routers acting as half-routers on a link with no network name.

sections.title: Implementation Notes
sections.content:
Implementers should be aware that ATCP packets cannot be exchanged until PPP reaches the network-layer phase. An implementation must be prepared to wait for authentication and link quality checks to complete before timing out waiting for configuration responses.

Unrecognized ATCP codes should trigger a Code-Reject response. The protocol field for ATCP is hex 8029; the protocol field for AppleTalk data itself is hex 0029.

Because AppleTalk has no standard fragmentation method, implementations must ensure the link can accommodate the full 599-octet maximum DDP datagram length in the PPP information field.
sections.eli5: Wait for the link to be ready before expecting ATCP negotiation, and make sure the connection can carry the biggest AppleTalk message without breaking it up.
